correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the PED condition for every unselected edge uv as d_F(u)+d_F(v)=1, since uv itself is not selected and selected edges incident at u and v are disjoint. Thus W={v:d_F(v)=0} is independent and F is exactly the edge set induced by V\W. If W is nonempty on one side, the universal twin class forces exactly one nonwhite vertex on the other side, yielding precisely a star centered in A_p or B_1. If W meets both sides, only the universal centers remain nonwhite, forcing a singleton edge; independence of the remaining vertices rules this out for p>=3 and forces p=2, alpha_2=beta_1=1. The p=1 complete-bipartite formulas deduplicate stars that coincide with E. The C++ checker and stored output were inspected at their actual package paths; its finite mask census is corroboration only, not the infinite proof.
residual_risks: The exhaustive checker was inspected, not rerun during this audit; its stated finite limits do not certify the theorem independently.

value.rationale: A connected chain graph is a natural nested-neighborhood class. The exact list of every PED-set and the full edge-cardinality polynomial expose an unusually sparse solution family and settle the precise boundary where an efficient edge dominating set exists. This is a self-contained structural classification, not merely a finite table or a new algorithm claim.
residual_risks: The classification may be a short corollary of the general coloring characterization, but the explicit all-solution structure and exception remain mathematically useful.

final_claim: The full PED family on a connected chain graph with canonical nonempty twin classes is E(G), the alpha_p stars centered in A_p, the beta_1 stars centered in B_1, plus the unique singleton edge exactly when p=2 and alpha_2=beta_1=1; the p=1 complete-bipartite case has the stated deduplicated polynomial.
limitations: Finite simple connected chain graphs with positive canonical twin-class sizes only.
The result gives an explicit structural classification; it does not claim a new algorithm for all P6-free graphs.
